title: Cloudy Sunset at CTIO
caption: Sunset over Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: An unusually rich, colorful sunset fills the sky behind NSF NOIRLab's Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory (CTIO). A small clamshell dome sits in the foreground, and a tall metal frame topped by a canvas dome stands in the background at left.

Clouds can make for a fine sunset, but water vapor in the atmosphere also hampers astronomy by absorbing starlight. Astronomers and engineers have built a set of instruments to measure the effect. The clamshell dome houses one of them, aTmCam, the Atmospheric Transmission Monitoring Camera. It is a new calibration system that tells astronomers how much light is getting through the atmosphere.

The frame at left belongs to another atmospheric instrument at CTIO, the DIMM2 Seeing Monitor. It runs automatically and measures seeing, the degree to which turbulence in the air blurs astronomical observations.

understand.summary: A sunset landscape photograph by B. Tafreshi. No camera or exposure details or color mapping are published.
understand.eye: Sunset colors are visible to the naked eye, though camera settings can change how strong they look in a photograph.

explore: The credit names the photographer as B. Tafreshi. Between them, aTmCam and DIMM2 track two different ways the atmosphere affects observations: how much light gets through, and how much turbulence blurs it.
